findings.title: Rounding-sensitive invoice math added with zero tests
findings.evidence: The whole class hard-codes a single money policy (scale 2, HALF_UP) and per-line rounding that determines the invoice total, but the diff adds no test class at all; no test commands were run, so the line-rounding and tax-rounding behaviour is entirely unverified.
findings.evidence_quote: private static final RoundingMode ROUNDING = RoundingMode.HALF_UP;
findings.recommendation: Add tests covering: a line price with 3+ decimals that forces HALF_UP (for example x.xx5), a quantity > 1 line, an empty item list (expects 0.00 with scale 2), subtotal + tax rounding at the half-cent boundary, and comparison against a sum-then-round reference to pin down the intended policy.

findings.title: totalWithTax validates nothing: null taxRate throws raw NPE, negative taxRate silently lowers the total
findings.evidence: LineItem's constructor rejects a null unitPrice with IllegalArgumentException, but totalWithTax accepts any taxRate: a null argument fails here with an unhelpful NullPointerException from BigDecimal.multiply, and a negative rate (say -0.1) is accepted and quietly reduces the invoice total.
findings.recommendation: Validate at the top of totalWithTax: require taxRate != null and taxRate.signum() >= 0 (or document refund/credit use and name the method accordingly), throwing IllegalArgumentException consistently with LineItem.

findings.title: Null list or null element yields an unhelpful NPE inside the loop
findings.evidence: The loop dereferences items and each element without a guard, so subtotal(null) and a list containing a null entry both throw a bare NullPointerException at iteration instead of a clear argument error, unlike LineItem which fails fast with IllegalArgumentException.
findings.recommendation: Add an up-front guard such as Objects.requireNonNull(items, "items required") (or throw IllegalArgumentException) and reject null elements in the loop before calling item.unitPrice().

findings.title: Quantity is constrained to > 0 but unitPrice may be arbitrarily negative
findings.evidence: The record enforces quantity > 0 but never checks the sign of unitPrice, so a negative price produces a negative line amount that flows into subtotal and totalWithTax, letting a bad caller produce a negative invoice total with a negative tax amount and no error.
findings.recommendation: Either reject unitPrice.signum() < 0 in the compact constructor (consistent with the quantity check), or explicitly document that negative prices model credits/discounts and add a test pinning that behaviour.
